title: お待たせしすぎたのかもしれません  (Perhaps I Kept You Waiting Too Long)

segments.t: Arriving late to a home appointment, Muranishi faces an annoyed client checking the clock. Instead of shrinking back, he delivers the line that becomes his lifelong trademark—turning his lateness into destiny and urging the room to decide right this instant. Listen to Muranishi at full power.
遅いわよ。約束の時間が過ぎてる。
申し訳ございません。お待たせしすぎたのかもしれません。
人との出会いはすべてミラクルです。
今決められないなら一生決められません。
皆様は毎日お忙しい日々を過ごしております。
ストレートに言います！
はっきり言ってラストチャンスです！
大勢の方がわたくしを待っているからです。
これはわたくしの使命なんです！
ジャストナウ！
俺、買うよ。今か！
ご購入ありがとうございます。今しかありませんよ！
Muranishi turns an ordinary sales visit into high theatre, culminating in his most famous catchphrase. Let's hear how each line lands.
遅いわよ。
'You are late.'  Starting off with
遅い
. This word covers both slow and late, and assertive
わよ
adds sharp impatience as she glares at the door.
約束の時間が過ぎてる。
'The appointment time has passed.'  The speaker uses
約束
this word means promise or appointment,
時間
is time, and
過ぎてる
comes from the verb for to pass beyond.
申し訳ございません。
"'I am deeply sorry.' Literally " We can hear

this word means an excuse or explanation, so saying none exists—
ございません
—declares 'my mistake is inexcusable'.
お待たせしすぎたのかもしれません。
"'Perhaps I kept you waiting too long.' Here is Muranishi's signature line! Polite " We can hear
お待たせ
, keeping you waiting, gets
しすぎた
. This word means too much, tucked inside—turning an ordinary late arrival into dramatic fate.
人との出会いはすべてミラクルです。
'Every meeting between people is a miracle.'  The character says
出会い
comes from the verb for to encounter by chance, naming a meaningful meeting in life, paired with
すべて
, all.
今決められないなら一生決められません。
'If you cannot decide now, you will not decide in a lifetime.'  We can hear
決められない
this word is the 'cannot decide' version of the verb for to decide, and
一生
spans one entire lifetime.
はっきり言ってラストチャンスです！
'To put it plainly, this is your last chance!'  The phrase contains
はっきり
is an expressive sound-word meaning clearly or bluntly, leading straight into katakana English

これはわたくしの使命なんです！
'This is my mission!'  It features
使命
this word means a calling or mission, and
なんです
wraps it in earnest conviction.
ジャストナウ！
"'Just now!' Muranishi shouts English " Pay attention to
ジャストナウ！
to mean 'right this very second!'—even though English speakers would say 'right now!'

"'I will buy it.' Swept up in the urgency, the buyer blurts plain dictionary-form " The word

. This word means to buy, plus decisive
よ

"'There is only right now!' Pairing " Listen for

, now, with negative

creates a spotlight meaning 'nothing except right now!' Now let's listen to Muranishi's legendary late-arrival pitch again.

Remember the phrase for an appointment time, the expression when you need a sincere formal apology, and the expression for 'there is only now!'. See you at the celebration next.
またね。
